head: claude/mi128-pnl-sweep-close-keyed
title: MI-128: key the local-pnl sweep's scan window on the CLOSE, not the OPEN
body:
**Tier-2 · landing: `hold` · DO NOT SELF-LAND.** `.github/pr-landing/mi128-pnl-sweep-close-keyed.json` declares it.

Fixes `BL-20260905-LOCAL-PNL-SWEEP-WINDOW-KEYS-ON-THE-OPEN-SO-A-LONG-HELD-CLOSE-IS-NEVER-PRICED`.

## The defect

`_sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced` bounded its scan with `datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now','-14 days')`. `created_at` is when the position was **OPENED**; the value the sweep exists to recover is a property of the **CLOSE**. A position held longer than the window is already outside it at the moment it closes and stays outside forever — so the row was never selected, never offered to the anchor, and **never reached the `no_anchor` branch that stamps `pnl_source: unmeasured`**.

The result was a *silent* NULL with no provenance key at all — the state `src/runtime/provenance.py` exists to prevent (*"absence of a provenance record is not evidence of measurement"*). Head of the chain whose tail proposes retiring real strategies: pnl NULL → absent from `/api/bot/performance` (its SQL carries `AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL`) → `sunset_pass` has no lifetime measurement → a retirement basis built on an absence.

## The diff

```diff
-    AND datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now', '-14 days')
-  ORDER BY datetime(created_at) DESC
+    AND datetime(COALESCE(closed_at, created_at)) >= datetime('now', '-14 days')
+  ORDER BY datetime(COALESCE(closed_at, created_at)) DESC
   LIMIT 100
```

**`ORDER BY` is re-keyed too** — flag this if you disagree, it is the one judgement call beyond the literal one-liner. It feeds `LIMIT 100`, so ordering by the OPEN leaves the same defect one level down: a long-held row that has just closed sorts last and would be starved behind 100 more-recently-opened rows. Not binding today (10 rows eligible vs a limit of 100), but it is the identical defect and leaving it would make the fix half-applied.

## Population — stated for every number below

`trade_journal.db::trades`, **all 5,494 rows fetched complete by pagination** via `/api/bot/db/table/trades` (`fetched == total_reported`), read 2026-09-05 against live trader `git_sha 9337958e`. Non-backtest, `status='closed'`, `intent_reduce` legs excluded, hold computable = **1,373 rows**. (The work object's baseline was 5,493/1,373 against `5eb59917`; one row has been added since.)

| hold bucket | n | pnl NULL | null % |
|---|---|---|---|
| < 1 day | 1103 | 22 | 2.0% |
| 1-7 d | 196 | 3 | 1.5% |
| 7-14 d | 47 | 12 | 25.5% |
| **> 14 days** | 22 | **20** | **90.9%** |

| | declared unmeasured | SILENT (no `pnl_source`) |
|---|---|---|
| held ≤ 14 d | 16 | 21 |
| held > 14 d | **0** | **20** |

Not one row held longer than the window has ever been declared — 0 of 20 — not because the anchor failed but because the sweep never asked. (The baseline read 15/22 on the ≤14d half; one row has since been declared, which is the sweep working on an in-window row and is a live positive control that it runs at all.) The only two >14d rows carrying a pnl were filled by *other* paths: `pairs_half_open_cleanup` and `bybit_closed_pnl` broker truth.

## The change is strictly additive — measured, not assumed

- **9 rows gain eligibility, 0 lose it.** The fix cannot remove coverage.
- **Every non-null `created_at` (5,494) and `closed_at` (1,625) parses under sqlite `datetime()` — 0 unparseable.** This is the regression I went looking for: if any `closed_at` were epoch-ms, `datetime(COALESCE(...))` would resolve NULL and *drop* a row the old predicate included. It cannot, on this population. The fail-safer alternative `COALESCE(datetime(closed_at), datetime(created_at))` was considered and rejected in favour of the form the work object, the backlog row and the test's own proposed-fix docstring all name — deviating would substitute my design for an approved one. If you would rather have the fail-safer form, say so and it is a one-line change.

## ⚠️ FORWARD-ONLY: what merging actually does

Merging **is** the deploy here (`ict-git-sync` pulls `main` every ~5 min), so this needs a decision, not just an approval.

Of the 9 newly-eligible rows, **4 already carry `pnl_source: unmeasured`** (the sweep takes the `already_unmeasured` branch and writes nothing), leaving **5 historical rows the first post-deploy tick would actually write**: `4169`, `4170` (alpaca TLT, 30.0d hold, both carry a recorded `exit_price` of 83.53 → local compute, not an anchor), `4422`, `4423` (alpaca IWM, 23.1d), `4484` (alpaca GLD, 17.8d). That is the same five the MI-127 diagnosis named — arrived at independently here.

Each would be filled by a sanctioned path: a recorded fill, a close-time anchor stamped ESTIMATED, or an explicit `unmeasured` declaration. **None can be fabricated** — the sweep's mark-to-market fallback was removed on 2026-07-30 and `bar_close_at` returns `no_anchor` rather than a substitute price. But it is still a back-fill of already-silent rows, and the FORWARD-ONLY condition reserves that to you. **No historical row was back-filled by this branch: it touches no database.**

## Re-measurement over the same population

The fix is not deployed, so these are two different measurements and are not conflated.

**(A) Forward — the property the fix buys.** Asking, for every row in the population, *"if this row closed now, would the sweep select it?"*: under the old predicate hold duration decided scannability for **27 of 1,373** rows (0% of the >14d bucket was scannable); under the new one it decides it for **0**. All four hold buckets reach 100%. A close is a close.

**(B) Historical — what forward-only leaves.** Of the 20 silent rows: **5** have closes inside the window and are what merging would reach; **15** closed more than 14 days ago and are outside *any* 14-day window forever. **This fix does not take the historical count to zero — 20 → 15, and only to 15 if you also accept the 5-row back-fill.** Reporting otherwise would be the dishonest direction, so those 15 are filed as a tracked residual (below) rather than left to be rediscovered.

## Done conditions

1. ✅ Strict-xfail marker and `test_long_hold_row_is_never_even_scanned` **removed**. The xfail XPASSing was the signal.
2. ✅ `test_the_scan_window_check_can_fail` (in `tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py`) now ages out **both** timestamps and is green. It had to change: ageing only `created_at` no longer removes the row, so it would have gone red while proving nothing.
3. ✅ Re-measured above. Every row held >14d that closes **from here on** is either priced or explicitly declared unmeasured — and the two stay distinguishable, which is the point.

**Surviving assertions**, so it is clear what still holds the line:
- `test_short_hold_row_is_priced` — positive control; a negative below is real, not a broken fixture.
- `test_the_window_predicate_keys_on_the_close` — structural pin, re-keyed. Now also asserts the open-keyed predicate is *absent* and that `ORDER BY` keys on the close. Normalised (comments dropped, quotes stripped, whitespace collapsed) so a cosmetic re-wrap can't redden it.
- `test_a_recent_close_is_priceable_regardless_of_hold_duration` — the acceptance criterion, now unmarked; strengthened to assert `scanned == 2`.
- **`test_a_long_held_close_is_never_silent`** (new) — pins the *other* terminal outcome: with the venue offering no bar, the row must come back carrying `pnl_source: unmeasured`. Done-condition 3 says both outcomes are acceptable and must stay distinguishable, so the declared branch is asserted directly rather than left to follow from the priced one.

## Verification

- **312 passed** across all 16 test files touching either sweep.
- **Both controls checked by mutation, not asserted.** Reverting the predicate to `created_at` reddens exactly the three MI-128 assertions. Deleting the window predicate outright reddens `test_the_scan_window_check_can_fail` — so the negative control genuinely can fail and is not vacuous.
- **`run_guards.py --base main`: PASS 67 · FAIL 0.** Note the first run reported 16 guards *not selected because the work was uncommitted* — guard relevance is computed from a commit range, so that run was not real coverage; the 67/0 is from the committed tree.
- **`layer-guard` passes for real.** The dispatch anticipated exit 127; I installed `import-linter` and ran it: *6 contracts kept, 0 broken*. I did check the 127 reproduces on a pristine `origin/main` worktree first, but actually running it is better evidence than matching an excuse. `ruff-lint` also ran and passed on this diff.

## Filed, not fixed

Three rows via `scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row` (never by hand; clean round-trip, +36 lines), each with `severity`, `tier`, `resolution_criteria` and its own population:

1. **`BL-20260905-BYBIT-BROKER-PNL-SWEEP-WINDOW-ALSO-KEYS-ON-THE-OPEN`** — a **recurrence of this exact class** in the sibling sweep `_sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit`, whose 7-day window is also measured from `created_at`. Worse than MI-128: Bybit's `closedPnl` is **MEASURED** broker truth retained ~7 days *from the close*, so a position held >7d loses a measured value where MI-128 lost an estimated one. 26 Bybit rows held >7d, 5 of them pnl NULL. **This interacts with the PR:** those 5 sit in the 20-row silent set, so once MI-128 deploys the local sweep can reach such a row and book an ESTIMATED price where a MEASURED one was available but never asked for.
2. **`BL-20260905-LOCAL-PNL-BROKER-DEFER-GRACE-KEYS-ON-THE-OPEN`** — the 6h `_LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS` grace that exists so local compute never pre-empts fee-accurate broker truth is *also* measured from `created_at`, so a row held longer than 6h has zero grace left when it closes. The function's docstring says it defers "once the broker reader has had its window"; the field does the opposite. Inert for **333 of 1,204** Bybit rows (27.7%). The row is explicit that this measures the *guard being inert*, not that 27.7% were mispriced — how often the race is lost is unmeasured. MI-128 makes this newly reachable.
3. **`BL-20260905-FIFTEEN-LONG-HELD-CLOSES-STAY-SILENT`** — the residual from (B). Filed to be *known*, not acted on: its `resolution_criteria` closes only on a recorded operator decision either way, and names *a session back-filling them on its own judgement* as the failure it exists to prevent.

## Not done, deliberately

- **No self-land.** Tier-2, and `pr-landing-guard` would refuse it anyway — I did not touch the guard that judges this PR.
- **No back-fill.** No database was written.
- **No VM mutation.** Diag/DB-explorer reads only.
- **Nothing outside `src/runtime/order_monitor.py`'s scan query** plus tests, the landing declaration, and the backlog.
